blocks.text: Special proteins produced in the liver make the complement system of proteins. This system consists of more than a dozen different proteins that circulate in the blood in an inactive state. When they encounter a microbe, they become active in a sequence. The first protein activates the second and so on. The final five proteins form a membrane-attack complex (MAC) into the plasma membrane of microbe. This complex punctures the plasma membrane of microbe. So, fluids and salts move inside microbe resulting in its swelling and bursting.

blocks.alt: A section of the microbe's membrane (a lipid bilayer) pierced by proteins of the membrane attack complex that line a channel. Arrows of fluid rush from outside, through the channel, down into the cytoplasm of the microbe.
blocks.caption: Figure 21.7: The Complement system of proteins and their functioning (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 21.7).
